hook_text: Push a rectangle and watch it turn into something else. Same sides, new name.
clip_script: Mr Dlamini's workshop in Soweto. A bookshelf frame: 80 cm by 50 cm, four right angles. A rectangle! Now push the top sideways. Whoa! The sides are still 80 and 50. Still parallel. But the corners slant. Two acute, two obtuse. It is a parallelogram! So every rectangle is a parallelogram, just a neat one. And the fix? One diagonal brace makes triangles, and triangles do not wobble.
visual_style: A wooden frame in a workshop leaning over in slow motion, with arrows marking parallel sides and angle arcs changing colour.
mood: Hands-on and clever, like a maker video.
pacing: Calm build, a dramatic push, then quick labels and the brace fix.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort the quadrilateral family.
